clue.text: One's experienced in mediaeval script

definitions.meaning: one who is experienced: a veteran, someone long practised at a job
handwriting of the Middle Ages, an antique hand or style of lettering

explanation.surface: A scholar who has long studied medieval manuscripts shows their expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions; it looks like a container signal but nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is called an old hand idiomatically, and an archaic style of handwriting is literally an old hand.

clue.text: Line not to be crossed means nothing to guerrilla

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter shrugs off a boundary he is told never to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link word. The OCHE is the line behind which a darts player must stand when throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the throwing line that players must not step over.

clue.text: Day holds nothing for a brave

indicators.note: the abbreviation for day contains, or holds, the word for nothing

parts.note: DY is an abbreviation for day
OUGHT is an old variant of nought, meaning nothing or zero

explanation.surface: A warrior finds there is nothing in the day for someone courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link. OUGHT as 'nothing' is a crossword favourite, a variant spelling of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty is an old-fashioned adjective for valiant, stout-hearted and fearless.

clue.text: Fire blows roof off old car

indicators.note: in a down answer the roof is the top letter, here blown away

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A blaze tears the roof off a battered old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a verb or a blaze, but it is the noun meaning passion or rage. BANGER is everyday British slang for a decrepit car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire in the sense of fiery temper or wrath is a synonym of rage.

clue.text: Useless people on the stage of Calamity Jane?

definitions.meaning: members of a group who contribute nothing and could be dropped

definitions.text: on the stage of Calamity Jane?
definitions.meaning: the ... Stage is the stagecoach song from the film Calamity Jane, the coach running to the Dakota town of that name

explanation.surface: Bad actors appear in a production of the musical Calamity Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests a theatre, but it is the stagecoach: 'The Deadwood Stage' is the famous song from the 1953 film Calamity Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadwood is an idiom for unproductive staff, and Deadwood is the frontier town served by the stagecoach in the film.

clue.text: Full of energy, return the box containing one health food

indicators.note: the reversed box wraps round the other pieces, containing them
return asks for the word for the box to be turned back to front

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV
one is the Roman numeral I
bran is a fibre-rich food associated with healthy eating

explanation.surface: Turn off the television that's showing a feature on a healthy breakfast cereal, and feel lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the box's letters back to front before they go round the rest. 'the box' is British slang for the television set; the comma is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrant describes something lively, pulsing with energy and vigour.

clue.text: Face struggle to fill up with fuel

indicators.note: the reversed fuel goes into the word for struggle, filling it

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle for something

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: gas is a fuel, also American for petrol

explanation.surface: A motorist has a hard time filling the tank with petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GAS into SAG, which is put into VIE; 'with' is a link. 'Face' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for a person's face or countenance.

clue.text: City's upcoming youngster wants Hearts transfer

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the city is what follows

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means the word rises, read backwards from the bottom

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

indicators.note: transfer signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A promising young footballer at a city club wants a move to Hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns CUB into BUC, and 'transfer' rearranges HEARTS into HAREST; 'wants' is a link. Hearts is the Edinburgh football club Heart of Midlothian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Quick way to deliver boy who will succeed, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear points to a word that sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: a son who will inherit the title is a male heir, or heir male

explanation.surface: A family wonders how to give birth to a son who will inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heir male' (a male heir, in legal word order) sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail sends letters by aeroplane, the speedy alternative to surface post.

clue.text: Mean to turn out for pageant

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone intends to appear at a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the ten letters of MEAN TO TURN; 'for' is a link. A mediaeval tournament was a showy contest of knights, hence pageant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament of jousting knights was a grand spectacle, a pageant of chivalry.

clue.text: Good figure, for an old timer

definitions.meaning: a curvy shape with a narrow waist, a classically shapely body
a device for measuring time with sand running between two glass bulbs

explanation.surface: An elderly person is admired for keeping a slim waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two definitions. 'old timer' looks like an elderly person, but it is an antique device that times things.
explanation.definitionFit: A curvaceous female shape is called an hourglass figure, and the sand-glass is an antique instrument for timekeeping.

clue.text: Wow! No end of good time in island

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for good time is removed

parts.note: fun is enjoyment, a good time

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the fun on holiday on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. COR is a British exclamation of amazement. 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it means the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Leaving for our regular holiday -—- how boring

definitions.meaning: what a family might cry setting off once more on the annual trip
an expression of weary exasperation at the same old thing happening again

explanation.surface: A family departs on the annual vacation, sighing at its tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase serves both: an excited cry on departure, and a groan at repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said both when setting off yet again and to show exasperated boredom at a repeat.

clue.text: Church festival is taken for granted

definitions.meaning: the feast on 15 August celebrating the Virgin Mary taken up into heaven
something supposed to be true without proof

explanation.surface: People expect a religious feast to happen as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Assumption is a Christian feast day, and a supposition accepted without proof is a premise.

clue.text: Broadcaster's plan to screen one that refers flippantly to minister

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite broadcaster

indicators.note: the word for plan goes round, screening, the next piece

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A TV company plans to show a programme that mocks a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that refers flippantly to' warns that the answer is a joking term, not a neutral synonym. 'to screen' looks like broadcasting but signals a container; the broadcaster is Britain's satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is jocular slang for a clergyman or chaplain, one who steers souls heavenward.

clue.text: Engine more durable than the Trojan one?

definitions.meaning: a railway locomotive, in old slang

definitions.text: more durable than the Trojan one?
definitions.meaning: the Trojan horse was wooden, so a metal one would last longer

explanation.surface: A machine is compared with the legendary wooden horse of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the wooden horse of Troy: a horse of metal would be tougher.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old nickname for a steam locomotive, and literally a horse made of metal.

clue.text: Uproar as old woman has heart transplant

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word for old woman are moved around

parts.note: a beldam is an archaic word for an old woman or hag

explanation.surface: An elderly lady causes chaos after a cardiac operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has heart transplant' swaps the middle pair L and D in BELDAM; 'as' is a link. BEDLAM was London's madhouse, hence uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum, means a scene of noisy chaos and confusion.

clue.text: The Mozart pack?

parts.note: split differently, the composer's first name reads as a band of predatory animals

explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's first name splits into a wild canine and a group, i.e. a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and a pack is a gang of wolves.

clue.text: Result perhaps of down being cold?

definitions.meaning: a downy game bird ends up cold, i.e. dead, when it is shot while flying high

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what happens when feathers get chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction, but it is feathers, standing for a bird; 'cold' means dead, as a bird is when shot in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: Hungry type needs second box

parts.note: a coffer is a chest or strongbox

explanation.surface: A ravenous person needs another container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is British slang for eating greedily, so a scoffer is someone who wolfs food down.

clue.text: Bunting on page in old map

indicators.note: in an across clue, the bird is placed on, i.e. after, the letter for page

parts.note: the ortolan is a small European bunting, a songbird

explanation.surface: Flags are draped on a page of an antique chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' looks like flags but it is the bird; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portolan was a mediaeval navigational chart showing coasts and harbours.

clue.text: Priest given torture not a proponent of evolution

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

indicators.note: not a means that the letter A is dropped from the combined pieces

parts.note: the rack is a medieval instrument of torture

explanation.surface: A clergyman subjected to torment is no believer in Darwinism.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMA + RACK gives LAMARACK; dropping one A ('not a') leaves the answer. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French naturalist who proposed an early theory of evolution.

clue.text: Airless rock in empty sky

indicators.note: the word for rock goes inside the remaining letters
empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the outer pair

parts.note: tuff is a rock formed from volcanic ash

explanation.surface: A heavy stone floats in a cloudless sky without wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves the first and last letters of sky, S and Y, round TUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room is badly ventilated, close and lacking fresh air.

clue.text: Jeremiah: "We want food, mother — pop out"

indicators.note: pop out suggests letters bursting out of order, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaining child demands to be fed by both parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FOOD, MOTHER and POP; 'We want' is a link. Jeremiah was the Old Testament prophet of disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jeremiah is a habitual pessimist, after the biblical prophet who foretold catastrophe.

clue.text: Brown gets right inside 1 dn

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is put inside the earlier answer

parts.note: the answer to 1 Down, the darts throwing line

explanation.surface: A colour gets put on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link. R goes inside the 1 Down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellowish-brown pigment and colour.

clue.text: Sloth, say, ignoring half the garden

indicators.note: the second half of the word for the animal group is left off

parts.note: the sloth is an example of an edentate, a toothless mammal

explanation.surface: Laziness, one of the deadly sins, neglects half the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the deadly sin, but it is the animal; 'say' signals an example. Dropping the half TATE leaves the answer; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden of the Bible where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Deduce one's heard to be wrapped up warmly

indicators.note: one's heard means the words that follow are said aloud and give a similar sounding word

parts.note: dressed in fur, i.e. in fur

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a person is bundled up against the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link. 'in fur' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to conclude or reason something out from evidence.

clue.text: Achievement to present head of dodo, thus?

definitions.text: Achievement to present head of dodo, thus?

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement
here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Displaying a dodo's head would be some accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The whole clue is the definition too: a dodo's head, like all of it, was covered in plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a bird, so it was covered in plumage like any other.

clue.text: An end of some tests to which children go

definitions.meaning: one end of Lord's cricket ground, where Test matches are played
a school or crèche for very young children

explanation.surface: A school term finishes with exams for pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tests' looks like exams, but it is Test cricket: Lord's in London has a Pavilion End and a Nursery End.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nursery End is at Lord's cricket ground, and a nursery is where infants are cared for.

clue.text: Good woman's family is often pickled

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning belonging to a woman
kin are one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: A virtuous lady's relatives are frequently drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' looks like British slang for drunk, but it is literal; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cucumber usually preserved in vinegar, served as a pickle.
